question: How does the analogy of the woman going to her lover clarify Shiva's regard for knowability?
premises: The woman restrains her own limbs thinking she will be seen.
Her action is guided by anticipated perception.
Shiva likewise regards the knowability of this for this.
inference: Anticipated knowability can shape action and cognition even before explicit perception occurs.
uncertainties: The exact referents of the two 'this' elements in 'this-knowability-of-this' are ambiguous in isolation.
plain_english: A woman going to her lover restrains her own limbs, thinking, 'He will see me.' In the same way, Shiva too regards this as knowable for this.
